review_notes: I read the whole file and the one downstream file that uses the definition, RegularisedComplexLinearVolterraUniqueness.lean. The definition is a plain `def` with no pointwise (`_apply`) lemma and no simp attributes. Its callers unfold it by name, so I report one modest finding. I did not check other possible simp lemmas for `regularisedTensorPhysicalMap`. I could not run Lean, so the finding is unverified by compilation.

findings.problem: The definition has no pointwise unfolding lemma, such as a `regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath_apply` that unfolds to `regularisedTensorPhysicalMap ρ ε hε (g (regularizedMildTimeClamp T hT s)) (v (regularizedMildTimeClamp T hT s))`. Nor is the linearity lemma `_sub` tagged `@[simp]`. Every user therefore has to unfold the whole definition by name. This file does so with `unfold` and `simp only [regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath, ...]`. The Volterra uniqueness file does the same at lines 168–169 and 173–174 (`simpa only [F, regularisedComplexShiftedStokesIntegrand, regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath] using hu q`). Unfolding by name exposes the clamp and the raw bilinear map, which is the unwanted expansion, instead of a stable interface term. The same file's `_norm_le` proof has to `change` the goal into `‖F (g q) (v q)‖` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath_apply (ρ ε hε T hT g v s) : regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath ρ ε hε T hT g v s = regularisedTensorPhysicalMap ρ ε hε (g (regularizedMildTimeClamp T hT s)) (v (regularizedMildTimeClamp T hT s)) := rfl`. A `simp only [regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath_apply]` or `rw` can then replace the unfold-by-name calls, and the `change` in `_norm_le` becomes unnecessary. Consider marking `regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath_sub` `@[simp]`. Its left side `... g (u - v) s` is a strictly simpler pattern than the right side, so it cannot loop. Its normal form pushes subtraction out to the tensor path.
findings.benefit: Callers get a single canonical, documented unfolding step that applies only when the path is evaluated at a point. They no longer unfold the definition wholesale. A `simp` call can also split `(u - v)` paths without being handed the definition name, which is what the uniqueness proof does by hand through `hsub`.
